subject: Scope & timing for activity snapshot and raw event export for SIG package
messages:
From: Marta Lewis <marta.lewis@crestline.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Crestline Procurement <procurement@crestline.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Snapshot: scope & preferred delivery window for SIG evidence

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. Our InfoSec team requested a scoped activity snapshot and raw-event export to attach to our SIG submission. They have three asks we need to scope:

1) Timebox: a 30-day window (Apr 1 - Apr 30) is what they prefer.
2) What event classes are included by default (admin console logins, API keys, role changes, model deploys, inference request metadata, workspace membership changes, operator overrides)?
3) Delivery: preferred format is something our auditors can ingest (ndjson or Parquet) and a signed manifest for chain-of-custody. Are you able to provide a presigned S3 delivery or do you host a temporary download?

Can you confirm feasibility and an ETA so we can align with procurement? I attached the SIG checklist for reference.

Regards,
Marta
Senior IT Risk Manager
Crestline Health

Attachment: crestline_sig_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Marta Lewis <marta.lewis@crestline.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot: scope & preferred delivery window for SIG evidence

Hi Marta — thanks, this is straightforward. Quick summary and proposal: 

- Inclusion: we can include the following event classes for the requested 30-day window by default:
  * Admin console logins (successful + failed)
  * API key creation/rotation/revocation
  * Role and permission changes (grant/revoke)
  * Model deploys and model version rollouts (who triggered, commit id)
  * Inference request metadata (request id, model, token counts, latency, anonymized prompt hashes)
  * Workspace/user membership changes and SSO events
  * Operator-led overrides (kill/restart, scale events)

- Redactions & privacy: free-text prompt content is not included by default in the raw activity export for privacy reasons; we provide hashed prompt IDs and a per-request token counts/latency. If you need full prompt text we need an additional DPA clause — let me know.

- Formats & delivery: we can deliver NDJSON (recommended for auditors), Parquet (compressed columnar), or CSV for summary tables. Delivery options: presigned S3 tarball (HMAC-signed manifest) or a time-limited HTTPS download hosted on our secure transfer endpoint. Both include SHA256 checksums in the manifest.

- Chain-of-custody: export will include a manifest (SHA256 checksums per file), an extraction log (timestamped extraction steps), and a PGP-signed summary if required by legal.

- Retention & sampling: Redwood retains full event ledgers for 90 days by default; we can pull a historical snapshot for the requested month even if it is older, but exports older than 365 days may require extended lead time. Aggregated metrics are retained longer (12 months).

- ETA & effort: small exports (<=100GB compressed) typically ship within 5 business days. Larger bundles (100GB-1TB) take ~10 business days for packaging and verification. Very large or cross-region extractions: up to 15 business days.

I'm copying Laura to flag billing/ingress egress costs and Olga for packaging/manifest ops. If that all looks good I'll schedule the extraction and we can provide a sample NDJSON file so your auditors can confirm ingest.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample-ndjson-extract-20270512.ndjson (text/vnd+ndjson)

From: Marta Lewis <marta.lewis@crestline.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot: scope & preferred delivery window for SIG evidence

Thanks — helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from our auditors:

- Can you confirm whether the inference request metadata includes client IPs and user agent strings? They want to map request origin for a subset of sessions.
- For the model deploys, can you include git commit ids or model artifact checksums?
- Are failed console actions (e.g., failed privilege escalation attempts) recorded separately from successes?

Also, procurement asked about cost — please include any one-time extraction fees or egress estimates so we can include in the PO.

Best,
Marta

On Wed, May 12, 2027 at 11:02 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi Marta — thanks, this is straightforward....

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Marta Lewis <marta.lewis@crestline.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot: scope & preferred delivery window for SIG evidence

Hi Marta — Olga from Ops. Quick answers: 

- Client IPs & user agents: we store client_ip and user_agent fields in the request telemetry for hosted API calls. For private deployments we can include whatever your deployment logged; for hosted we can provide client_ip at the request level in the export. If you need IPs masked/pseudonymized we can do that as part of the extraction.

- Model artifact linkage: we store model artifact checksums and deploy metadata (commit id or artifact sha256) for all models in the catalog. We'll include the artifact checksum where available.

- Failed console actions: yes — failures are logged with a result field (success/failure) and an error_code when applicable. The export will surface both successful and failed actions.

Packaging notes: our NDJSON schema includes a top-level event_type, timestamp (ISO8601), actor (internal_id, email), target (resource_type, id), and metadata (flattened). Example event lines are included in the sample file I attached.

I'll start the extraction plan once procurement confirms the PO and we have a delivery window. Can you confirm whether SSO has to be included for the same timebox?

—Olga
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Marta Lewis <marta.lewis@crestline.com>, procurement@crestline.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot: scope & preferred delivery window for SIG evidence

Hi Marta / procurement team — Laura here (Finance). A few commercial points: 

- One-time extraction fee: $1,250 up to 100GB compressed (includes manifesting and PGP signing).
- Egress estimate: ~ $0.09/GB for outbound transfer, we will provide an estimated final invoice once we calculate the bundle size.
- SLA: packaged exports include a verification window (we checksum and keep a copy for 30 days). Any re-extract requests due to customer change requests are billable at a reduced rate.

If procurement can confirm PO # and whether you prefer presigned S3 or secure HTTPS transfer, we'll queue the work. Typical lead time after PO is 5 business days for the size you described.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Finance Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marta Lewis <marta.lewis@crestline.com>

All good — procurement confirmed PO CREST-2027-889 and prefers presigned S3 delivery. Please proceed with the Apr 1–30 window, include client_ip and artifact checksums, and keep prompt text redacted (hashed IDs are fine). We accept the one-time fee.

Can you send the export manifest and a sample NDJSON line so our auditors can do a test ingest before the full bundle?

Thanks everyone — appreciate the responsiveness.

Marta
